answer: Practically, the chain should score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because wander only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, kernel is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any tundra approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
